note: Shrink-only, same contract as config/tmp-leak-baseline.json. These are the source files that a test under tests/ mentions and that day mode can select NO SPECIFIC TEST for: neither the import route nor the string-literal route reaches them. Each was traced by hand to the site that reaches it; the reason below says which mechanism, so a reader can tell a real hole from a coincidental word match. Nine of the ten are reached by a tree sweep that IS in the mandatory core and therefore does run on every day-mode invocation, which is why day mode is safe over them today; they are recorded here because the sweep is a tree-wide invariant check and not a test of the file's behaviour, and because a sweep's glob can be narrowed later without anything saying so. Adding an entry is a deliberate act and the wrong first move: when tests/test_day_mode_blind_spot.py goes red, look first at whether the literal route can be taught the shape the new test uses, because every shape it learns closes the hole for every future file at once.

reasons.scripts/migrations/0001_baseline.py: THE ONE GENUINE HOLE OF THE TEN, and the shape worth reading. It is NOT swept by tests/test_import_purity.py, whose glob is 'scripts/*.py' and stops one level above scripts/migrations/. It is exercised by tests/test_five_reports_that_outran_their_evidence.py, which calls registered_migrations() from scripts/migrations/__init__.py; that function discovers the module with pkgutil.iter_modules and loads it with importlib.import_module(f'{__name__}.{name}'). The module name is assembled at run time from a discovered string, so neither an import edge nor a literal exists anywhere for day mode to find. A change to this file selects no test that runs it.
